details:
[Version]

Windows 11

Unity 6000.0.67.f1

SDK 3.11.0-beta.1

The following errors are encountered when viewing inspectors that contains the `<a>` or `<u>` richtext tags surrounding non `en-US` glyphs. I encountered the issue while creating localization files for UI Toolkit assets. This is a new issue happening only in Unity 6, and is happening regardless of additional language packs / editor language preference.

When the issue is produced, the console is spammed with errors and all inspectors part of the affected GUI pane break, forcing the user to close the affected GUI pane entirely by closing all windows in the pane.  Modifying the inspector to remove the `<a>` or `<u>` richtext tags and opening a new GUI pane and inspector resolves the issue entirely.

Some things to note:

- The errors can be replicated on a blank Unity 6 Avatar Project by inputting non `en-US` glyphs in UI Builder with `<a>` or `<u>` richtext tags.

- This is a new issue in Unity 6, using packages exported from Unity 2022.3.22f1 that work as intended.

- This does not happen when viewing the `en-US` characters, which further makes me believe it could be a font-lacking issue on my part, or may be indicative of a change in how Unity 6 implements underline text generation.

The issue can be mitigated by enabling the new Advanced Text Generator (ATG) in `Project Settings -> UI Toolkit -> Advanced Text Generator`, and setting the newly accessible `Text Generator Type` to `Advanced` in the UI Builder. While ATG is enabled by default in Unity 6.5+, it is still an experimental feature in Unity 6.0; for that reason I am doubtful to consider it a potential solution.

The issue can be resolved completely by changing the Editor Font in `Preferences -> General -> Editor Font` to `System Font` instead of `Inter (Default)`, but that may entirely depend on the enduser's system font.

Part of my intention of posting this here is to see if the issue is affecting non `en-US` users as well. I have been going back and forth on implementing a regex replace layer on my UI to remove `<u>` tags, and replace `<a>` tags with the new `<link>` richtext tag, to at least maintain compatibility with Unity 2022.3.
